classification.difficultyReason: Convert eight exponential inequalities to logarithmic bounds, preserve inequality direction for bases greater than one, and calculate bounds to three significant figures.

content.prompt: Rewrite each inequation in terms of logarithms, with $x$ as the subject. Then use the change-of-base formula to solve it, giving your answer correct to three significant figures.

answer.worked:
Since $2>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&>\log_2 12\\x&>\frac{\log_{10}12}{\log_{10}2}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}12}{\log_{10}2}=3.584962\ldots$. Hence $x>3.58$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.

Since $2>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&<\log_2 100\\x&<\frac{\log_{10}100}{\log_{10}2}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}100}{\log_{10}2}=6.643856\ldots$. Hence $x<6.64$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.

Since $2>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&<\log_2 0.02\\x&<\frac{\log_{10}0.02}{\log_{10}2}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}0.02}{\log_{10}2}=-5.643856\ldots$. Hence $x<-5.64$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.

Since $2>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&>\log_2 0.1\\x&>\frac{\log_{10}0.1}{\log_{10}2}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}0.1}{\log_{10}2}=-3.321928\ldots$. Hence $x>-3.32$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.

Since $5>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&<\log_5 100\\x&<\frac{\log_{10}100}{\log_{10}5}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}100}{\log_{10}5}=2.861353\ldots$. Hence $x<2.86$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.

Since $3>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&<\log_3 0.007\\x&<\frac{\log_{10}0.007}{\log_{10}3}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}0.007}{\log_{10}3}\approx-4.5163$. Hence $x<-4.52$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.

Since $1.2>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&>\log_{1.2}10\\x&>\frac{\log_{10}10}{\log_{10}1.2}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}10}{\log_{10}1.2}=12.629253\ldots$. Hence $x>12.6$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.

Since $1.001>1$, the inequality direction is preserved.
$$\begin{align*}x&>\log_{1.001}100\\x&>\frac{\log_{10}100}{\log_{10}1.001}\end{align*}$$
The boundary is $\dfrac{\log_{10}100}{\log_{10}1.001}=4607.472387\ldots$. Hence $x>4.61\times10^3$, with the boundary rounded to three significant figures.
